title: Game loop and win check
idea: The game loop asks the current player's strategy for a move, applies it, and stops when the new move completes a line or fills the board.
points: Each turn: ask the current `MoveStrategy`, apply the move, check, pass the turn.
Players are the Strategy pattern from c08, so new types never touch the loop.
A win can only appear on lines through the last move: O(n) work.
Counters per row, column and diagonal make the check O(1) and undo trivial.

code.title: Loop with strategies
code.caption: A scripted player against a bot. The loop only knows the `MoveStrategy` interface.

walk.text: One contract for every kind of player: given a board, return a move.
A scripted strategy stands in for a human. Tests use the same trick.
The bot is a strategy too. A smarter bot is a new class, not a loop change.
Each turn hands over a deep copy, so a buggy strategy cannot edit the board.
The move is placed. Real code runs the model page's rule checks first.
Two exits: a win on the new move, or a full board for a draw.
Only the row, column and two diagonals through the move are scanned: O(n) per move.

code.title: O(1) check and undo
code.caption: An N-by-N extension: running sums per line give an O(1) win check and a cheap undo.

walk.text: One counter per row and column, plus two diagonals. Memory is O(n), not O(n²).
X adds +1 and O adds -1, so a line reaches ±n only when one symbol fills it.
Each move updates at most four counters, whatever the board size.
A win is any counter whose absolute value equals n.
Undo subtracts the same move. A scanning design would have to recompute.
X's anti-diagonal win is taken back, then O completes the main diagonal.

pitfalls: Passing the live array to a strategy lets a buggy bot overwrite cells; pass a copy.
Forgetting the draw exit makes the loop ask for a move on a full board.
Reusing counters for k-in-a-row with k < n reports wins for non-adjacent marks.

quiz.q: Extension: a 5x5 board where four in a row wins. Which win check is correct?
options: Keep line counters, but win at absolute value 4
Count adjacent marks out from the last move, four directions
Check only the two diagonals through the last move
Test whether each player's last four moves line up
quiz.why: A row counter sums the whole row, so gaps still count. Walking out from the new move counts only adjacent marks, in each of the four line directions.

takeaway: Loop over strategies, check only the last move's lines, stop on win or draw.
